title: Oceania capitals four of four · Fiji, Australia and New Zealand
edition: Oceania capitals · Four regional lessons · John · November 2026
intro: Welcome to the Oceania capitals, episode four of four. First, I clear the chosen names for a fresh regional lesson.
And three close the series: Fiji, and the two great southern states of Australia and New Zealand.

states.name: Suva
lines: Suva stands on a peninsula on the south-east coast of Viti Levu, the largest island of Fiji.
The capital since 1882, it is one of the largest towns of the South Pacific islands, and the University of the South Pacific, founded here in 1968, serves twelve countries.
Remember Suva as the university that serves a twelfth of the Pacific, on the peninsula of Viti Levu.

states.name: Canberra
lines: Canberra stands inland in the south-east of Australia, between Sydney and Melbourne, in the Australian Capital Territory.

From a Ngunnawal word, probably "meeting place"; built as a compromise capital because Sydney and Melbourne could not agree, and designed by an American who won a competition, its street plan is a set of geometric axes aligned to the surrounding hills.
Remember Canberra as the compromise capital between two rival cities, laid out in geometric axes for the hills.

states.name: Wellington
lines: Wellington stands on the southern tip of the North Island of New Zealand, on the harbour of Cook Strait.
Named for the Duke of Wellington, it is the southernmost capital of a sovereign state, and it is known as Windy Wellington for the gales that come through the Strait.
Remember Wellington as the windiest of the capitals, and the southernmost of them all.

recap: Suva stands on a peninsula of Viti Levu in the north of the group, Canberra inland between Sydney and Melbourne, and Wellington at the southern tip of the North Island.
Remember the university that serves a twelfth of the Pacific, the compromise capital laid out in geometric axes, and the windiest and southernmost of the capitals.
